_provenance_note: Every parameter carries a quality tag in `provenance`. `hard` = taken directly from a sourced research observation in data/raw/. `calc` = arithmetic on sourced observations, with the formula stated. `assumption` = a modelling judgement that could NOT be sourced in this session (the web-search budget was exhausted mid-research); these are the parameters to attack first when stress-testing the model, and they are listed together in `assumptions`.

baseline._comment: Pre-war reference levels (late Feb 2026), against which scenario prices are differenced.

cross_price._comment: Elasticity of each product price to a proportional Brent move, used when the sensitivity grid and the interactive controls scale prices off crude. Set to near-unity because in a chokepoint event the same physical constraint drives all four; they are assumptions, not estimated betas.

scenarios.label: De-escalation
scenarios.description: A shipping-protection accord or ceasefire restores roughly half of pre-war transit. Prices fall back but stay above pre-war on a persistent risk premium.

scenarios.label: Current grind (base)
scenarios.description: The state observed on 2026-09-14: transit at a small single-digit share of normal after the East-West pipeline shutdown, Brent above $100, price support still in force in both economies.

scenarios.label: Full closure
scenarios.description: Transit near zero and sustained, with Gulf loading infrastructure damaged. Substitution and reserve draw are both maxed out, so the residual must be rationed.

scenarios.label: Full closure, support withdrawn
scenarios.description: As full closure, but fiscal price support lapses under budget pressure. The retail price signal is restored, so more demand adjusts voluntarily and reserves last longer — at the cost of a much higher CPI print and a larger real-income hit.

baseline.brent_usd_bbl.basis: Brent averaged $71/bbl on 2026-02-27, the last pre-strike session.

baseline.jkm_usd_mmbtu.basis: JKM $24.685/mmbtu on 2026-09-09 (hard), reported +118% y/y, so pre-war = 24.685 / 2.18.

baseline.naphtha_usd_t.basis: Level not sourced; only the +60% change (2026-04-30) was found. Round pre-war level assumed.

JP.macro.nominal_gdp_usd_bn.basis: Structural baseline not captured by the research workstreams; standard magnitude used.

JP.energy.oil_imports_via_hormuz_kbd.basis: 2,360 kb/d x 94.1% Gulf/Hormuz share (both sourced) = 2,221 kb/d.

JP.energy.oil_demand_kbd.basis: Total oil product demand not sourced; standard magnitude used.

JP.energy.lng_import_mt_yr.basis: Tonnage not sourced this session; only the -3% y/y change was found.

JP.reserves.usable_stock_mnbbl.basis: ws5_runway: 247 mn bbl usable = national reserve in full plus private stock drawable down to the reduced 55-day obligation.

JP.reserves.max_deliverable_draw_kbd.basis: Physical draw-and-deliver ceiling; not published. This binds before stock size does and is the single most important assumption in the Japan runway.

JP.reserves.policy_max_draw_kbd.basis: Political willingness to draw; not published.

JP.mitigation.max_substitution_kbd.basis: Hormuz share fell 94.1% -> 59.3% by Jul 2026 (both sourced); 34.8% x 2,360 kb/d = 826 kb/d of demonstrated substitution.

JP.elasticities.oil_demand_price_elastic.basis: -0.05 short-run price elasticity of oil demand (EIA working paper, ws3_elasticities).

JP.elasticities.tot_transfer_to_gdp_mult.basis: Per-$10/bbl GDP elasticities could not be sourced for either economy (recorded NA in ws3_elasticities). This converts the measured income transfer into a GDP effect.

JP.elasticities.gdp_pp_per_pct_involunta.basis: Output cost of rationing, deliberately set well above the terms-of-trade coefficient because rationing destroys production rather than transferring income.

JP.cpi.energy_weight_pct.basis: CPI basket energy weight not sourced this session.

JP.cpi.retail_energy_passthrough.basis: Share of a wholesale energy move reaching retail prices.

JP.cpi.naphtha_to_cpi_beta.basis: Indirect pass-through via packaging, plastics and processed goods; no quantified coefficient could be sourced.

JP.policy.cpi_suppression_pp.basis: Aggregate Japanese energy-subsidy effect on headline CPI estimated at -1.0 pp (ws4_policy).

JP.policy.subsidy_passthrough_block.basis: Fraction of the retail price signal blocked by subsidy, which is what suppresses voluntary demand response.

JP.policy.gdp_support_pp.basis: Demand support from the fiscal package.

CN.macro.nominal_gdp_usd_bn.basis: Structural baseline not captured by the research workstreams.

CN.energy.oil_demand_kbd.basis: 11,000 kb/d imports + 4,300 kb/d domestic production (both sourced) = 15,300 kb/d of supply, used as the demand proxy.

CN.energy.oil_imports_via_hormuz_kbd.basis: 11,000 kb/d x 36.1% Gulf/Hormuz share (both sourced) = 3,971 kb/d.

CN.energy.lng_import_mt_yr.basis: 100 bcm of LNG imports (sourced) / 1.36 bcm per mt = 73.5 mt.

CN.reserves.usable_stock_mnbbl.basis: ws5_runway: 750 mn bbl usable commercial stock after an assumed 25% tank-bottoms floor. China does not publish reserve data, so this rests on commercial estimates.

CN.mitigation.max_substitution_kbd.basis: Hormuz-dependent 3,971 kb/d less the realised import shortfall (11,000 - 8,930 = 2,070 kb/d in Aug 2026) = 1,901 kb/d replaced, largely by Russian and Central Asian pipeline barrels.

CN.elasticities.oil_demand_price_elastic.basis: EIA short-run elasticity, as for Japan.

CN.elasticities.tot_transfer_to_gdp_mult.basis: Set below Japan's because China's price caps and state-absorbed refining losses blunt the pass-through to households.

CN.cpi.energy_weight_pct.basis: Not sourced; set below Japan's, consistent with a lower direct fuel weight in the Chinese basket.

CN.cpi.retail_energy_passthrough.basis: Lower than Japan's because the NDRC pricing mechanism caps pass-through by design.

CN.policy.cpi_suppression_pp.basis: Effect of the NDRC price mechanism; not separately quantified in the sources found.

CN.policy.subsidy_passthrough_block.basis: Price-cap blocking of the retail signal.

assumptions: Per-$10/bbl GDP elasticities could not be sourced for Japan or China; the GDP channel therefore runs off a measured income transfer times an assumed multiplier rather than a published elasticity.

Reserve deliverability ceilings are unpublished for both economies and are assumed. In most scenarios deliverability, not stock size, is what binds — so this assumption drives the runway more than the reserve totals do.
CPI energy weights, retail pass-through and the naphtha beta are assumed; only Japan's aggregate subsidy effect on CPI (-1.0 pp) is sourced.
Nominal GDP levels and Japan's oil demand and LNG tonnage are standard magnitudes, not figures verified against a source in this session.

Product prices are scaled off Brent with near-unity betas in the interactive grid; in reality naphtha and LPG have moved further than crude in this episode, so the grid understates the petrochemical channel.
China's reserve position rests on commercial estimates throughout, since no official data is published.
